column1: # and what the downstream contract owes for it. Enforced by the SV-CONTRACT-CURRENCY doctrine
# ⛔ WHY IT EXISTS, measured not imagined: between 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-19 the SV grammar shipped
# SEVEN semantically-distinct revisions while the contract kept saying `1.0.183`. The leaf that
# opened to fix that debt tracked the population BY HAND and its table went stale twice more inside
# the same week — `-0232` and `-0233` landed and were never added, so `-0237` was routed as "the
# FIFTH change" when it was the SEVENTH commit and the FIFTH to move a verdict. A hand-kept list of
# accept-set changes is the same object as the debt it tracks.
# semantic_digest = sha256 of the EBNF FRONTEND'S OWN `raw_ast` envelope — what the code generator
# consumes, from which comments are absent by construction. Re-derive:
# ⛔ To a FILE, never /dev/stdout — the tool writes progress there too and the JSON parse fails.
# ⛔ THE KEY IS THE DIGEST, NOT THE COMMIT. The first design keyed rows on the commit sha and had a
# chicken-and-egg the very next grammar change exposed: the row for the commit being made cannot
# carry that commit's own sha. The digest is known BEFORE the commit is, and it is the identity the
# contract actually describes, so `commit` is documentation and may be back-filled.
# disposition: RELEASE = the contract carries a section and the bug ledger carries a row.
#              NEUTRAL = comment-only; the digest EQUALS its predecessor's, which is what the
#              doctrine checks, so the claim refutes itself when false.

column7: GENESIS — the last revision the contract described before this register existed (ledger SV-0053, schema 20 -> 21)

.13c.2d — cross_body_item_sv_2017 matched the LRM's MISSPELLED nonterminal as a literal keyword; WIDEN sv_2017 + AST-SHAPE (cross_body items lose their per-item [item, semi] pair) => ledger SV-0054, schema 21 -> 22
.13c.2f slice 4 — the two PATHPULSE$ tokens were transliterated to the word `_dollar`; WIDEN + NARROW on all three profiles => ledger SV-0055, schema 22 unchanged

.13c.2c — a negative lookahead that could never pass made the hierarchical receiver loop run ZERO iterations; WIDEN all three + AST-SHAPE (a hierarchical call's path moves out of method_call.chain) => ledger SV-0056, schema 22 -> 23
.13c.2j — three inline copies of A.8.4's scope prefix never received the class_scope branch; WIDEN sv_2017+sv_2023 => ledger SV-0057, schema 23 unchanged
.13c.2o — IEEE 1800-2023 covergroup inheritance needed the LRM's FOOTNOTE NUMBER typed into the source; WIDEN + NARROW sv_2023 => ledger SV-0058, schema 23 unchanged

.13c.2q + .13c.2r — eight gate/switch keywords lost their trailing DIGIT and a greedy star starved a mandatory tail; AST-SHAPE only, all three profiles (udp_instantiation -> gate_instantiation) => ledger SV-0059 + SV-0060, schema 23 -> 24
a re-derivation under director challenge rewrote one comment block; digest byte-identical to its predecessor, and no pinned witness moved on either axis

.13c.2k + .13c.2t — a reserved keyword parsed in every NON-FINAL hierarchy component, and assignment_pattern_key was narrower than §10.9.2's own example; NARROW all three + AST-SHAPE => ledger SV-0061 + SV-0062, schema 24 -> 25
a second re-derivation under director challenge rewrote two comment blocks; digest byte-identical to its predecessor, and no pinned witness moved on either axis

.13c.2s — a greedy `( X )*` in front of an OPTIONAL X-shaped tail, at FOUR sites: a system task/function call could never reach its clocking-event argument, and the let/property/sequence argument lists could never reach a NAMED argument after a positional one; WIDEN sv_2017+sv_2023 => ledger SV-0063 + SV-0064, schema 25 unchanged

SV-0065 (.13c.2v slice 1 diagnosed, slice 2 landed) — IEEE 1800 A.8.4 spells `primary`'s call alternative `function_subroutine_call`, which A.8.2 expands to include `[ std :: ] randomize_call`; PGEN rendered it as `call_primary`, whose eleven alternatives carry no `randomize_call`, so the `with constraint_block` tail of a SCOPE randomize was unreachable from EVERY expression while the statement and constant paths both had it. Lifted as profile-gated `scope_randomize_sv_only`, referenced as the LAST alternative of `primary_sv_2017` and `primary_sv_2023` (position is part of the fix: every part of `randomize_call` is optional, so an earlier placement captures a bare `randomize` used as a user identifier, which IEEE 1800 Annex B permits)

SV-0066 (.13c.2y) -- an IEEE 1800 KEYWORD was bound to the ARROW token of the same name: `implies := trivia "->"` predated the extraction of A.2.10, so `a implies b` was REJECTED at every release while `-> b` and `a |= b` parsed as properties. Minted kw_implies_470cec58 (profile-gated SV-only) and moved the operator to its Table 16-3 precedence group prop_until_*, deleting three defect branches from both prop_primary_*. WIDEN + NARROW on sv_2017+sv_2023; verilog_2005 byte-inert. Schema 25 -> 26 (three prop_primary kinds removed). Side effect: the deleted alternative was the ONLY left-recursive one in prop_primary, so the property_expr indirect-LR knot dissolved -- census 1611 -> 1516, parser -8.41 MB, cert union UNKNOWN 53 -> 1.

SV-0068 (.13e.5) -- IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.7 makes a task/function port DIRECTION mandatory (task_port_item is one of three tf_*_declarations, each BEGINNING with its keyword), and PGEN carried the IEEE 1800 shape (direction optional) on ALL profiles, so `task t(a, b);` parsed as plain Verilog. NARROW on verilog_2005 only: `tf_port_item`/`tf_port_list` split into profile-gated variants; the sv_2017/sv_2023 body is a byte-for-byte re-spelling. ⛔ The obvious fix (a direction on EVERY item) was built, regenerated and MEASURED rejecting `task t(input integer a, b);`, which A.2.7:300 DERIVES -- one `input` covers a list_of_port_identifiers -- so the shipped shape admits a directionless item only when it is a BARE port identifier and requires the FIRST item to carry a direction. Schema 26 unchanged (both variants emit the identical 5-field return; ast_shape_contract 18/18, drift 0).

SV-0069 (.13e.4) -- IEEE 1364-2005 puts NO signing on an integer or a time declaration: A.2.1.3 integer_declaration:152 and time_declaration:174 are `<kw> list_of_variable_identifiers ;`, A.2.8's block forms :314/:315 are the same, and neither `signing` nor `integer_atom_type` appears anywhere in that Annex. PGEN spelled `data_type` and `block_data_type` the IEEE 1800 way -- `integer_atom_type ( signing )?` -- with NO @profiles gate, so `integer unsigned u;` / `time signed t;` parsed as plain Verilog at module, block, function and task scope. NARROW on verilog_2005 only. ⭐ THE GATE GOES ON THE OPTIONAL, NOT ON THE ALTERNATIVE: unlike SV-0068, the rule beside it (`integer_atom_type`) MUST stay reachable under verilog_2005 -- that admission is what makes plain `integer i;` parse -- so the .13e.5 _sv_only/_v2005 split is the wrong idiom here. One new rule `integer_atom_signing_sv_only := signing` @profiles [sv_2017, sv_2023], referenced inside the optional at both sites: no data_type alternative added, no branch index moved, `signing: $2` keeps its slot and is simply always absent under verilog_2005. ⛔ The routing evidence understated the defect TWICE and one command said so each time -- `time` is the same atom (integer_atom_type admits exactly integer + time under this profile) and `block_data_type:2077` is a second byte-identical site. Schema 26 unchanged (the sv_2017 typed AST is byte-identical across the edit, proven on 11 inputs by --interpret-parse-ast-json BEFORE any codegen).

SV-0070 (.13e.7) -- IEEE 1364-2005 admits none of thirteen IEEE-1800 surfaces the verilog_2005 profile was still reaching, and the population was MEASURED over a closed set rather than listed: `chandle`/`enum`/`string`/`virtual interface` types (each occurs 0x in Annex A; `string` is the A.8.8:1218 LITERAL, never a type), the `const`/`var` qualifiers and the DATA-declaration and MODULE-header `lifetime` (A.2.1.3:152 carries no qualifier and no lifetime; A.1.2:29 no lifetime at all), `extern` on a module or UDP header, `default disable iff`, `fork join_any` / `join_none` (A.6.3 par_block:529 -- `join` is the ONLY terminator), the checker `rand` qualifier, the array-method `with` clause, and the whole streaming concatenation (`{ << { a } }`, which no keyword-level lens can see because `<<` and `>>` are OPERATORS). Fixed with the named `_sv_only` idiom at 19 v2005-live sites plus one whole-rule gate on `streaming_concatenation`; `lifetime` itself stays UNGATED because A.2.6:254 / A.2.7:275 give function/task a legitimate `[automatic]`. ACCEPT-SET NARROW under verilog_2005 ONLY: sv_2017 and sv_2023 are byte-identical (each gate is a bare pass-through alias and the reference site keeps its return annotation), ast_shape_contract 18/18 with the AST schema UNCHANGED, sv_cert union total 1388->1401 / union_witness 1380->1393 (+13 = exactly the rules added) with union_unknown still 0.
